chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Anyone who believes in God and the Last Day should not leave shaving his pubic hair for more than forty days. If he does not find [a razor], let him borrow [one] after the forty days and not delay.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time limit for shaving pubic hair in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal codifies the Sunnah of Qada al-Ha'ath (removing body hair) within a forty-day lunar cycle, linking personal hygiene directly to faith in the Hereafter. It highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence by permitting the borrowing of tools if one lacks the means, thereby removing financial hardship as an excuse for delay. This ruling underscores the importance of cleanliness (Taharah) as a prerequisite for worship and spiritual purity.
